While some companies are choosing to renew their executive leadership to drive operational changes, others have opted to retain their Chief Executive Officers (CEOs) for over 30 years, betting on long-term vision and results.

Among the companies listed in the Mexican Stock Market's Price and Quotations Index (IPC), 15 organizations have maintained the same CEO for more than a decade.

These executives have notably been pivotal in their companies' expansion across sectors such as telecommunications, mining, retail, and transportation.

Megacable, Grupo México, and Chedraui: CEOs with over 30 years in the role

Megacable tops the list of companies with the longest-serving CEO. Enrique Yamuni Robles has been at the helm for 44 years; he founded the company in 1982 and has led it ever since.

During his tenure, Yamuni Robles has overseen Megacable's transformation from a cable television provider to a company offering integrated telecommunications services, internet, and fiber optics.

Another notable case is Grupo México, a conglomerate involved in mining, rail, and infrastructure, led by Germán Larrea Mota-Velasco — one of the wealthiest men in the country — for 32 consecutive years, from 1994 to the present.

In the retail sector, José Antonio Chedraui Eguía has served as CEO of Chedraui for approximately 31 years. He took on the role in 1995 at the age of 28, succeeding the previous generation of the family, led by Antonio and Alfredo Chedraui Obeso.

Since then, the company has expanded its presence both in Mexico and the United States through openings and acquisitions, including Carrefour México, Fiesta Mart, and Smart & Final.

América Móvil and Pinfra: over two decades of the same leadership

The longevity of CEOs is also notable in the infrastructure and telecommunications sectors. América Móvil has been headed by Daniel Hajj Aboumrad since 2000, when it began operations following its split from Telmex.

With 26 years in leadership, Carlos Slim Helú's son-in-law has guided one of the leading telecommunications firms in Mexico and Latin America, focused on mobile and fixed-line telephone services, internet, and pay television.

In the infrastructure sector, David Peñaloza Alanís has directed Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura (Pinfra) since 2001, when he took over the leadership of the then Grupo Tribasa during its restructuring process.

Subsequently, between 2005 and 2006, the company returned to the stock exchange and officially adopted the name Pinfra. Today, Peñaloza Alanís also serves as the chairman of the board.

Other CEOs with over a decade of tenure

The list of CEOs with significant tenure also includes companies with a strong presence in their respective economic sectors, such as airlines, financial institutions, and consumer goods companies.

Currently, the following CEOs have maintained their positions:

  • Enrique Beltranena has led Volaris since 2006.
  • Pablo González Guajardo has been at the helm of Kimberly Clark México since 2007.
  • Adolfo Castro Rivas has directed ASUR since May 2011.
  • Javier Foncerrada Izquierdo has headed Grupo Financiero Inbursa since 2012.
  • Juan Antonio González Moreno has been with Gruma since December 2012.
  • Marcos Ramírez Miguel has led Grupo Financiero Banorte since November 2014.
  • Antonio Gómez García has been at the forefront of Grupo Carso since April 2014.
  • Enrique Escalante Ochoa has been with GCC since 2015.
  • Enrique Majos Ramírez has led Gentera since August 2017.
  • Juan Domingo Beckman Legorreta has directed Becle since 2002.

(ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 11th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 11th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste SAB de CV is the trade name used on the Mexico Stock Exchange and Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. is used on the New York Stock Exchange.

NEWS BITES - PRIVATE COMPANIES (US)

+ ATLAS RENEWABLE ENERGY [3 Press Releases]

+ PENOLES AND ATLAS RENEWABLES STRIKE 20-YEAR SOLAR AND STORAGE DEAL IN COAHUILA

MEXICO CITY, Nov. 18, 2026 -- Penoles and Atlas Renewable Energy have agreed to a 20-year deal to build a solar generation and storage project in Coahuila, delivering 550 GWh per year from 269 MWp of solar plus a battery system. The project will begin operations in the first half of 2029, supporting Penoles' decarbonization goals and providing flexibility for its energy-intensive operations in northern Mexico. The package includes Clean Energy Certificates CELs and capacity provisions designed to diversify Penoles energy sources and reduce long-term costs. Atlas says this marks its first renewable energy supply contract with a private client in Mexico and expands its regional presence. The deal is expected to deliver emissions reductions of about 244,000 tons of CO2e per year and to contribute to local hiring and Coahuila's supply chains.

+ PENOLES TEAMS WITH ATLAS RENEWABLE ENERGY TO EXPAND RENEWABLE FOOTPRINT WITH A 20-YEAR MEXICO PROJECT

Penoles has entered into a 20-year contract with Atlas Renewable Energy to develop a solar generation and storage project in Coahuila, comprising 269 MWp of solar capacity and a battery storage system designed to deliver about 550 GWh annually. Operations are slated for the first half of 2029.

The arrangement adds energy storage to its solar supply, enabling better management of the electricity supply profile for an industrial operation with continuous demand.

The project will include Clean Energy Certificates and capacity, contributing to long-term flexibility and the decarbonization strategy, with estimated avoided emissions around 244,000 tons of CO2e per year.

Atlas Renewable Energy notes this is its first renewable energy supply contract with a private client in Mexico, expanding its regional experience across mining, metals, chemical, cement and technology sectors.

+ PENOLES INKS LONG-TERM RENEWABLE POWER PACT WITH ATLAS, TARGETING 550 GWH/YEAR VIA SOLAR AND STORAGE

MEXICO CITY, Nov. 18, 2026 -- Penoles and Atlas Renewable Energy have agreed to a 20-year renewable energy supply deal to build a solar generation and storage project in Coahuila. The facility comprises 269 MWp of solar capacity with a battery storage system and is planned to deliver about 550 GWh per year.

The project will supply part of Penoles' electricity demand in northern Mexico, supporting its strategy to increase renewable energy use and add storage for industrial flexibility. The arrangement includes Clean Energy Certificates and capacity to ensure reliability and long-term cost-competitiveness. Construction is slated to start, with operations expected in the first half of 2029.

Penoles' 2025 Sustainability Report shows that 49.9% of its electricity came from renewables, and the project is expected to avoid approximately 244,000 tons of CO2e annually, advancing the company's decarbonization goals. Atlas notes that this contract marks its first renewable energy supply agreement with a private client in Mexico, expanding its regional portfolio across multiple sectors. Local hiring and supply chain development in Coahuila are anticipated as Atlas develops the project.

SECTION 7 CORPORATE PROFILE

7.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 11th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste SAB de CV is the trade name used on the Mexico Stock Exchange and Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. is used on the New York Stock Exchange.

SECTION 7 CORPORATE PROFILE

7.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 11th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

While market concerns such as slowing consumer spending and rising commodity costs persist, Coca-Cola FEMSA's fundamentals remain compelling. Jul 05, 2026: Coca-Cola Femsa Expands Beverage Operations for Long-Term Growth

Coca-Cola Femsa S.A.B. de C.V., the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the world by volume, continues to leverage its wide Latin American footprint and franchise agreements to drive beverage distribution and long-term growth opportunities. As of the 5th of July, 2026, Coca-Cola Femsa's operations underline a robust business model focused on efficiency and localized strategies that resonate with regional consumer preferences.

Coca-Cola Femsa oversees a broad network of bottling plants and distribution centers that support a high-frequency, high-volume beverage business in both emerging and developed Latin American economies. Its territories include key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, and other countries in Central and South America, where population density and urbanization provide a large consumer base for ready-to-drink beverages. The company manages operations spanning manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, and last-mile delivery to retailers, restaurants, and other points of sale.

The company operates under long-term franchise and bottling agreements that define its rights and obligations to produce, market, and sell Coca-Cola branded beverages in assigned territories. Within this framework, Coca-Cola Femsa focuses on operational efficiency, portfolio management, and local commercial strategies while coordinating with the brand owner on marketing and innovation. This strategic approach allows the company to combine globally recognized brands with local knowledge of consumer preferences and retail formats.

Beyond classic colas, Coca-Cola Femsa manages a broad beverage portfolio that typically includes flavored sparkling soft drinks, still juices, sports drinks, teas, and bottled water. The company adapts flavors, package sizes, and multipack configurations to local consumer tastes and price points, ensuring a tailored approach that meets diverse market demands. Packaging innovation plays a central role in Coca-Cola Femsa's operations, as the company strives to meet sustainability expectations and improve efficiency.

From an investor perspective, Coca-Cola Femsa is often viewed as a consumer staples business with exposure to multiple Latin American currencies and macroeconomic environments. Analysts closely monitor capital expenditure commitments, leverage metrics, and dividend policies when assessing the balance between growth investment and shareholder returns. For many global investors, Coca-Cola Femsa represents an opportunity to tap into Latin American consumer trends through a well-established beverage platform tied to iconic soft drink brands.

Jun 23, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Launches 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle to Enhance Family Consumption

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle, targeting family consumption in key Mexican markets. This launch, taking place on 23rd June 2026, is a significant step in the company's strategy to enhance the availability of reusable packaging solutions.

The Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle is designed for households that prefer purchasing beverages in bulk while maintaining the option for return and reuse. This innovative format not only aims to reduce packaging waste but also lowers the per-liter cost for consumers, who can return the bottle to local corner stores, which have long embraced returnable formats.

Mariana Rodriguez, product manager at Coca-Cola FEMSA, noted that the bottle features a more pronounced waist and a textured grip, enhancing usability at family gatherings. The design is lighter than traditional glass returnable bottles, making it easier for all family members, including children and seniors, to handle. While glass maintains a nostalgic appeal, the PET format provides a modern balance of convenience and tradition.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's CEO, John Santa Maria, has emphasized the importance of refillable packaging as a core strategy. The new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle aligns with the company's sustainability goals, as using refillable containers can significantly reduce the carbon footprint associated with beverage consumption. This initiative not only supports environmental efforts but also fosters a culture of reuse among consumers.

Initially available in select Mexican markets, the Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle leverages the existing popularity of refillable formats. The pricing structure typically includes a deposit for the bottle, making it economically advantageous for families who purchase large quantities. This strategic move is expected to positively impact Coca-Cola FEMSA's long-term cash flow and shareholder value, as the company continues to adapt to consumer preferences while committing to sustainable practices.

Jun 17, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Leverages Logistics-as-a-Service to Enhance Distribution

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. is quietly enhancing its distribution capabilities through Fomento Economico Mexicano's Logistics-as-a-Service offering. This innovative service transforms FEMSA's robust Coca-Cola delivery network into a third-party logistics solution for brands requiring efficient, temperature-controlled distribution across Mexico. This strategic move was made public on the 17th of June, 2026, and is expected to reshape the logistical landscape in the region.

FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service fundamentally allows third-party brands to access the same warehousing, routing software, and last-mile fleet utilized by Coca-Cola in Mexico and other Latin American markets. Clients can seamlessly integrate into FEMSA's extensive delivery network, which significantly reduces the need for them to establish their own complex logistics operations. This means that consumer goods can be efficiently delivered to over 3 million points of sale, utilizing existing routes that serve thousands of small retail outlets daily.

For brands, especially those in the fast-moving consumer goods sector, this service provides an invaluable shortcut to market penetration. Products delivered alongside Coca-Cola benefit from the established distribution patterns that store owners are accustomed to, thus facilitating easier acceptance and integration into existing supply chains. The service's reach can substantially expedite market entry for new energy drinks or healthcare products, compressing lengthy rollout periods into mere months.

Technological infrastructure underpins this service, with advanced routing algorithms and inventory management tools ensuring efficient operations. FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service also offers clients features such as order tracking and delivery proof without necessitating additional investment in software. This is particularly crucial for pharmaceuticals and health products, where stringent temperature control and delivery reliability are essential.

Logistics-as-a-Service is a strategic component of FEMSA's broader vision to maximize value from its existing infrastructure. Although still a smaller segment compared to its core Coca-Cola bottling and OXXO retail operations, it represents a significant opportunity for growth. Investors should note that while immediate scale may be limited, the long-term potential for operating leverage in this logistics venture aligns with FEMSA's overarching objective of enhancing its distribution capabilities.

The returnable glass bottle operates on a deposit-return system, where consumers pay a deposit upon purchase and reclaim it when they return the empty bottle. In the markets where Coca-Cola FEMSA operates, these bottles are commonly found in traditional trade outlets, including neighborhood stores, small groceries, and food-service channels, coexisting alongside one-way PET bottles and cans.

For Coca-Cola FEMSA, the returnable glass bottle is not merely a product but a strategic asset that caters to price-sensitive consumers while enhancing the company's sustainability narrative around refillable packaging. SECTION 7 CORPORATE PROFILE

7.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

SECTION 7 CORPORATE PROFILE

7.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

MEXICO CITY, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Penoles, a major player in Mexico's mining and metallurgical sector, has announced a 20-year renewable energy supply agreement with Atlas Renewable Energy to support its decarbonization strategy through a solar generation and battery storage project in Coahuila. The project is expected to begin operations in the first half of 2029 and was disclosed in a company press release highlighting a commitment to sustainability and energy efficiency in industrial operations.

Under the terms of the deal, Atlas will construct a facility with 269 MWp of solar capacity, complemented by a battery storage system, designed to deliver about 550 GWh of electricity annually, enough to power roughly 317,000 Mexican households. The storage component provides Penoles with greater flexibility to manage its continuous industrial energy needs and advances its objective to raise the share of renewables in its energy mix.

Atlas Renewable Energy notes this marks its first long-term supply agreement with a private client in Mexico and expands its footprint in Latin America, where it serves across mining, metals, chemical, cement and technology sectors. Penoles' 2025 Sustainability Report shows nearly half of its energy consumption already originates from renewable sources, and the project is expected to cut carbon emissions by about 244,000 tons annually.

The agreement also aims to spur local development. Atlas expects to generate local jobs and foster supplier opportunities during project development and construction in Coahuila, aligning with sustainability and corporate social responsibility goals of both companies. Camilo Serrano, Atlas Mexico Country Manager, described the contract as a strategic demonstration that solar plus storage can offer a competitive option for Mexico's industrial sector moving forward.

+ ATLAS RENEWABLE ENERGY [3 Press Releases]

+ ATLAS RENEWABLE ENERGY SIGNS 20-YEAR AGREEMENT WITH PENOLES TO EXPAND SOLAR AND BATTERY STORAGE IN COAHUILA

MEXICO CITY, Nov. 18, 2026 -- Penoles, one of Mexico's leading mining and metallurgical groups, and Atlas Renewable Energy have signed a 20-year renewable energy supply agreement to develop a solar generation and storage project in the state of Coahuila. The facility will deliver 269 MWp of solar capacity paired with a battery storage system and is designed to supply about 550 GWh per year to Penoles. Operations are slated to begin in the first half of 2029, marking a major step in Penoles' plan to increase its use of renewable energy and to strengthen the energy competitiveness of its processes. The package includes renewable energy, Clean Energy Certificates CELs, and capacity arrangements that aim to lower energy costs while improving operational reliability across Penoles' northern Mexico operations. Atlas Renewable Energy notes that this is its first renewable energy supply contract with a private Mexican client, expanding its regional footprint after long-standing work with large buyers in mining, metals, chemical, cement and technology sectors. The company has built an asset base of more than 10.8 GW in Latin America and emphasizes ESG criteria and local development. Penoles' 2025 Sustainability Report shows that 49.9% of its electricity came from renewable sources, and the new supply is estimated to avoid about 244,000 tons of CO2e per year. The volume is equivalent to the annual electricity consumption of more than 317,000 households. The agreement also supports the development of local hiring and supply chains in Coahuila during its construction and operation.

+ ATLAS RENEWABLE ENERGY TO DELIVER 269 MWP SOLAR AND BATTERY STORAGE TO PENOLES UNDER 20-YEAR PACT IN COAHUILA

Penoles and Atlas Renewable Energy have signed a 20-year renewable energy supply agreement to develop a solar generation and storage project in Coahuila, featuring 269 MWp of solar capacity and a battery storage system that will deliver about 550 GWh per year to Penoles' northern Mexican operations.

The deal broadens Atlas's footprint among large energy users in Latin America, including mining, metals, chemical, cement and technology companies.

The integrated solution includes renewable energy, Clean Energy Certificates (CELs) and capacity to provide better flexibility and reliability for an energy-intensive operation.

Penoles has been pursuing renewable energy since 2025; its sustainability report shows 49.9% of electricity consumed came from renewable sources. The contract is expected to avoid about 244,000 tons of CO2e per year.

Atlas notes that this is its first renewable energy supply contract with a private client in Mexico, expanding its regional track record; the project will also seek to create local hiring and train local suppliers in Coahuila.

+ ATLAS RENEWABLE ENERGY TO SUPPLY PENOLES WITH 269 MWP SOLAR AND BATTERY STORAGE UNDER 20-YEAR CONTRACT

MEXICO CITY, Nov. 18, 2026 -- Penoles, a leading Mexican mining and metallurgical group, and Atlas Renewable Energy have signed a 20-year renewable energy supply agreement to develop a solar generation and storage project in Coahuila. The facility will include 269 MWp of solar capacity paired with a battery storage system and is expected to deliver about 550 GWh of electricity annually, sufficient to power more than 317,000 homes.

The arrangement will help Penoles diversify its energy mix and add storage-enabled flexibility for its operations. The bundled solution comprises renewable energy, Clean Energy Certificates and capacity to support long-term energy competitiveness while enabling a more reliable supply. Construction is planned to begin, with operations targeted for the first half of 2029.

Penoles' 2025 Sustainability Report shows the company obtained 49.9% of its electricity from renewable sources, and the project is estimated to avoid about 244,000 tons of CO2e per year, furthering its decarbonization efforts. Atlas Renewable Energy notes that this is its first renewable energy supply contract with a private client in Mexico, expanding its regional footprint across the mining, metals, chemical, cement and technology sectors. The project is expected to spur local hiring and training in Coahuila and bolster the state's supply chains as Atlas develops and implements the project.

6.1 Activities

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V., is a leading beverage company and the largest franchise bottler for The Coca-Cola Company in Latin America, headquartered in Mexico. Its core business revolves around the production, distribution, and marketing of a diverse portfolio of non-alcoholic beverages, including sparkling drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and energy drinks, primarily under the Coca-Cola brand. The company operates in key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, and Guatemala, utilizing an extensive supply chain and distribution network to reach consumers efficiently. Among its fastest-growing segments are still beverages, particularly flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, fueled by rising demand for healthier and functional options amid shifting consumer preferences. This growth is supported by strategic investments in innovation, sustainability, and digital platforms, positioning Coca-Cola FEMSA as a resilient player in the competitive beverage industry. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 14th largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Fresnillo PLC (LSE:FRES) and Pan African Resources PLC (LSE:PAF, OTCQX:PAFRY, JSE:PAN) helped lead a turn in London's precious metals market as investors rotated back into gold and silver stocks after a difficult week. On Nov. 23, 2026, Fresnillo rose 2.42% to 2,203p, while Endeavour Mining PLC (LSE:EDV, TSX:EDV, OTCQX:EDVMF) gained 1.70% to 3,228p.

Pan African Resources jumped 3.37% to 98.15p, and Meridian Mining Plc (LSE:MNO, TSX:MNO, OTCQX:MRRDF) advanced 3.48% to 71.4p, underscoring renewed interest in the sector. Spot gold climbed about 1.9% to $3,605 per ounce, with silver up roughly 2% as bargain hunters returned to bullion and miners. The previous week saw gold slide roughly 9% amid stronger U.S. data, persistent inflation and rising expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes that strengthened the dollar. A softer dollar on Monday, along with a reassessment of the rate outlook, encouraged investors to revisit mining stocks. London's benchmark indices also recovered modestly, with the FTSE 100 up 0.57% at 10,404.85 and the FTSE 250 up 0.71% at 23,819.87. UBS analysts cautioned that gold could retrace toward $3,500 before rebounding, but see a path to $5,000 by the end of 2027, making the upcoming U.S. inflation data a critical driver for precious metals and the miners that benefit from this rebound

About Finance of America Companies

Finance of America Companies, Inc., which operates as Finance of America, is a specialty finance company focused on home-equity solutions. Its core business is reverse mortgage lending, which enables eligible homeowners to access a portion of their home equity while continuing to live in their homes, subject to loan terms and borrower obligations. The company offers government-insured Home Equity Conversion Mortgages (HECMs) and proprietary reverse mortgage products, including jumbo loans. Its offerings also include reverse mortgages used to purchase a home.

About Grupo Financiero Banorte SAB de CV

Grupo Financiero Banorte is a Mexico-based financial services group whose principal banking subsidiary is Banco Mercantil del Norte, commonly known as Banorte. Its roots trace to Banco Mercantil de Monterrey, founded in 1899, and the group has grown through acquisitions and expansion in Mexico. Banorte offers personal and commercial banking services, including deposit accounts, loans, credit cards, payments and digital banking. Its other businesses provide services such as retirement savings and pension management, insurance, brokerage, investment and asset management, and leasing and factoring.

5.1 Activities

Arca Continental SAB de CV, a prominent Mexican conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages as a key franchise partner for The Coca-Cola Company. The company operates across Mexico, the United States, and South America, offering a diverse portfolio that includes carbonated soft drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and snacks. Its core activities encompass manufacturing, logistics, and sales through an extensive network of distribution channels, serving both retail and hospitality sectors. In recent years, the fastest-growing segments have been healthier beverage options, such as flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, driven by shifting consumer preferences toward wellness and hydration products. Additionally, international expansion into markets like Ecuador and Peru has fueled growth, enhancing revenue streams and market share. Arca Continental's strategic investments in sustainability and digital technologies further support its operational efficiency and long-term competitiveness in the global beverage industry. It is Mexico's largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

Ejecutivos de Arca Continental, Xignux y Nestlé México propusieron establecer una política industrial a largo plazo que trascienda los ciclos electorales, fortalezca las cadenas de suministro nacionales y permita al país atraer nuevas inversiones ante los incentivos ofrecidos por otras economías. Durante la Reunión Anual de Industriales 2026, Jorge Humberto Santos Reyna, presidente del Consejo de Arca Continental, enfatizó que para lograr este objetivo se requieren tres elementos clave: infraestructura, talento y certeza empresarial. Señaló que la disponibilidad de trabajadores calificados es un obstáculo para el crecimiento industrial, ya que Nuevo León necesita entre 40,000 y 50,000 nuevos técnicos cada año, mientras que las instituciones educativas solo forman entre 4,000 y 5,000. Destacó la importancia de promover la educación dual, que permite a los jóvenes combinar su formación académica con experiencia práctica en empresas.

David Garza Herrera, director de Asuntos Corporativos de Xignux, indicó que el crecimiento económico del país ha superado el desarrollo de su infraestructura, especialmente en el sector eléctrico. Explicó que la saturación de nodos en la red de la Comisión Federal de Electricidad (CFE) limita la expansión de actividades productivas y sugirió aumentar la capacidad de las líneas de transmisión existentes utilizando nuevas tecnologías. Fausto Oliveira Costa, presidente ejecutivo de Nestlé México, argumentó que los cambios fiscales recurrentes complican la planificación financiera de las empresas y propuso ampliar la base tributaria para evitar que la carga recaiga sobre quienes ya operan en la economía formal.

Santos Reyna también advirtió que la reubicación de negocios, conocida como nearshoring, no garantiza el crecimiento sostenido de la economía mexicana por sí sola, por lo que es esencial fortalecer el mercado interno. Detalló que aproximadamente el 95 por ciento de la cadena de valor de Arca Continental en México proviene de las regiones en las que opera y destacó que, a través de un programa de la Cámara de la Industria de Transformación de Nuevo León, se realizan transacciones por más de 400 millones de dólares anuales con pequeñas y medianas empresas. Sostuvo que una cadena de suministro sólida no se construye buscando siempre al proveedor más barato, sino desarrollando mejores proveedores.

Durante la Reunión Anual de Industriales 2026, Jorge Humberto Santos Reyna, presidente del Consejo de Arca Continental, enfatizó que para lograr este objetivo se requieren tres elementos clave: infraestructura, talento y certeza empresarial. Señaló que la disponibilidad de trabajadores calificados es un obstáculo para el crecimiento industrial, ya que Nuevo León necesita entre 40,000 y 50,000 nuevos técnicos cada año, mientras que las instituciones educativas solo forman entre 4,000 y 5,000. Destacó la importancia de promover la educación dual, que permite a los jóvenes combinar su formación académica con experiencia práctica en empresas.

David Garza Herrera, director de Asuntos Corporativos de Xignux, indicó que el crecimiento económico del país ha superado el desarrollo de su infraestructura, especialmente en el sector eléctrico. Explicó que la saturación de nodos en la red de la Comisión Federal de Electricidad (CFE) limita la expansión de actividades productivas y sugirió aumentar la capacidad de las líneas de transmisión existentes utilizando nuevas tecnologías. Fausto Oliveira Costa, presidente ejecutivo de Nestlé México, argumentó que los cambios fiscales recurrentes complican la planificación financiera de las empresas y propuso ampliar la base tributaria para evitar que la carga recaiga sobre quienes ya operan en la economía formal.

Santos Reyna también advirtió que la reubicación de negocios, conocida como nearshoring, no garantiza el crecimiento sostenido de la economía mexicana por sí sola, por lo que es esencial fortalecer el mercado interno. Detalló que aproximadamente el 95 por ciento de la cadena de valor de Arca Continental en México proviene de las regiones en las que opera y destacó que, a través de un programa de la Cámara de la Industria de Transformación de Nuevo León, se realizan transacciones por más de 400 millones de dólares anuales con pequeñas y medianas empresas. Sostuvo que una cadena de suministro sólida no se construye buscando siempre al proveedor más barato, sino desarrollando mejores proveedores.

Executives from Arca Continental, Xignux, and Nestlé Mexico proposed establishing a long-term industrial policy that transcends electoral cycles, strengthens national supply chains, and enables the country to attract new investments in the face of incentives offered by other economies. During the 2026 Annual Meeting of Industrialists (RAI), Jorge Humberto Santos Reyna, Chairman of Arca Continental's Board of Directors, emphasized that achieving this goal requires three key elements: infrastructure, talent, and business certainty. "We cannot be solving energy or water capacity needs year after year. A long-term plan is required to ensure we have the capacity to attract those investors and for us, as Mexican industrialists, to have certainty that we will have sufficient capabilities to continue expanding our companies," he stated. The businessman pointed out that another obstacle to industrial growth is the availability of skilled workers, noting that Nuevo León alone requires between 40,000 and 50,000 new technicians each year, while educational institutions are only training between 4,000 and 5,000. In light of this situation, he highlighted the importance of promoting dual education, which allows young people to combine their academic training with practical experience in companies, enabling them to earn up to 25 percent more upon completing their studies.

Electrical Saturation Limits Industrial Expansion. Meanwhile, David Garza Herrera, Director of Corporate Affairs at Xignux, stated that the country's economic growth has outpaced the development of its infrastructure, particularly in the electrical sector. "Economic growth has undoubtedly advanced much faster than the creation of infrastructure. We may be victims of our own success," he expressed. He explained that the saturation of various nodes in the network operated by the Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) poses a constraint on the expansion of productive activities. He suggested that one alternative is to increase the capacity of existing transmission lines using new technologies, utilizing available towers and rights-of-way, without the need to initiate the processes involved in building infrastructure from scratch. Additionally, he considered it necessary to establish economic incentives to compete for capital in the face of the United States, where Xignux has received support from state governments for its investments.

Nestlé Calls for an Expanded Tax Base. Fausto Oliveira Costa, Executive President and CEO of Nestlé Mexico, argued that recurrent fiscal changes complicate financial planning for companies since industrial projects are undertaken with long-term horizons. He proposed expanding the tax base to prevent the burden of government revenue needs from falling on those already operating within the formal economy. In this regard, he emphasized that the complexity of tax mechanisms creates costs that are difficult for companies to anticipate, as well as uncertainty regarding their future obligations to the Tax Administration Service (SAT). "If you ask, 'How much will SAT charge you in five years?' No idea," he stressed.

Internal Market, Key to Strengthening the Industry. Santos Reyna also warned that the relocation of businesses, known as nearshoring, does not guarantee the sustained growth of the Mexican economy on its own, making it essential to strengthen the internal market. He detailed that about 95 percent of Arca Continental's value chain in Mexico comes from the regions in which it operates. Furthermore, he highlighted that through a program by the Nuevo León Chamber of the Transformation Industry (Caintra), which includes 26 major companies, transactions exceeding $400 million annually are conducted with small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). "A strong supply chain is not built by always locating the cheapest supplier. It is built by developing better suppliers," he affirmed. He suggested that increasing domestic content would strengthen productive chains and facilitate compliance with the trade requirements of the products exported by Mexico.

Jul 20, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte's Growth Strategy Emphasizes Sustainability and Innovation

In an exclusive interview, Mr. Jose Luis Munoz, Executive Director of Sustainability & Investor Relations at Grupo Financiero Banorte, outlined the bank's strategic position for sustainable growth. The discussion, held on the 20th of July 2026, highlighted Banorte's financial performance amid a dynamic economic landscape and its commitment to fostering long-term sustainability.

Reflecting on Banorte's 125-year legacy, Munoz emphasized that the definition of a strong bank has evolved with changing economic and geopolitical landscapes. 'Resilience has been a hallmark of Banorte's history,' he explained, noting the bank's ability to navigate various challenges, including the rise of fintech competitors and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. This resilience is evident in the bank's growing loan portfolio, particularly in consumer lending, which saw an increase in mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.

The bank's commitment to the SME sector remains a cornerstone of its strategy, with dedicated resources aimed at improving customer interaction and service. Munoz explained that Banorte's extensive branch network, particularly in economically active regions, positions it favorably to cater to the needs of SMEs. The bank's approach to 'hyper-personalisation' through advanced technology and analytics further differentiates it from competitors, allowing for tailored offerings that resonate with customer needs.

Banorte's financial health is underscored by a robust capital adequacy ratio of 20.06%, well above regulatory requirements. Munoz highlighted the importance of maintaining a safety buffer due to the bank's status as a systemic institution without foreign subsidiaries. This focus on capital preservation, coupled with disciplined risk management, has enabled Banorte to sustain its strong liquidity position and support growth initiatives.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of Banorte's operations, with initiatives such as the commitment to plant one million trees by 2030 and participation in the Task Force on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD). Munoz noted that these efforts not only enhance the bank's sustainability practices but also help clients navigate risks associated with nature and biodiversity. As Banorte continues to expand its influence in the financial sector, its commitment to innovation, customer experience, and sustainable practices positions it as a key player in Mexico's economic development.

Jul 02, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte Strengthens Its Position in Mexico's Banking Sector

Grupo Financiero Banorte continues to position itself as one of Mexico's largest banks, combining a traditional branch network with digital services as it competes for retail and corporate customers in a changing rate and regulatory environment. As of 2nd July 2026, Banorte operates in an environment shaped by domestic interest rates, economic growth, and evolving regulation.

Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. (ISIN MXP370641013) is one of Mexico's largest financial groups, with activities spanning commercial banking, consumer finance, asset management, insurance, and pension funds. As a major lender in the Mexican market, the group plays a central role in financing households and businesses across the country. Its nationwide branch and ATM network supports a wide retail franchise, while its corporate and government banking units provide services to larger clients and public entities.

Management attention at Banorte typically centers on maintaining a balance between growth and risk, especially in areas such as consumer credit, mortgages, and small-business lending. Asset quality indicators, such as non-performing loans and coverage ratios, are closely watched, as they show how well the bank is managing credit risk in its portfolio. Additionally, capital adequacy remains a key concern, with banks expected to hold sufficient capital buffers to absorb potential losses and comply with regulatory requirements.

Banorte has invested in digital channels to complement its traditional branch network, offering online and mobile banking for individuals and businesses. These platforms allow customers to make payments, transfer funds, and apply for products such as credit cards and personal loans without visiting a branch. The ability to migrate more activity to digital channels helps Banorte improve efficiency by reducing operating costs per customer while maintaining or even expanding its customer base.

Banorte's shares are listed in Mexico, providing investors exposure to the country's financial sector through a diversified banking and financial services group. The stock's performance over time reflects local macroeconomic conditions, interest rate trends, and the bank's own profitability and risk management decisions. For equity investors, key variables often include return on equity, cost-to-income ratios, asset growth, and dividend policy, all of which shape how the market values Banorte relative to both domestic peers and international financial groups.

Jul 20, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte's Growth Strategy Emphasizes Sustainability and Innovation

In an exclusive interview, Mr. Jose Luis Munoz, Executive Director of Sustainability & Investor Relations at Grupo Financiero Banorte, outlined the bank's strategic position for sustainable growth. The discussion, held on the 20th of July 2026, highlighted Banorte's financial performance amid a dynamic economic landscape and its commitment to fostering long-term sustainability.

Reflecting on Banorte's 125-year legacy, Munoz emphasized that the definition of a strong bank has evolved with changing economic and geopolitical landscapes. 'Resilience has been a hallmark of Banorte's history,' he explained, noting the bank's ability to navigate various challenges, including the rise of fintech competitors and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. This resilience is evident in the bank's growing loan portfolio, particularly in consumer lending, which saw an increase in mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.

The bank's commitment to the SME sector remains a cornerstone of its strategy, with dedicated resources aimed at improving customer interaction and service. Munoz explained that Banorte's extensive branch network, particularly in economically active regions, positions it favorably to cater to the needs of SMEs. The bank's approach to 'hyper-personalisation' through advanced technology and analytics further differentiates it from competitors, allowing for tailored offerings that resonate with customer needs.

Banorte's financial health is underscored by a robust capital adequacy ratio of 20.06%, well above regulatory requirements. Munoz highlighted the importance of maintaining a safety buffer due to the bank's status as a systemic institution without foreign subsidiaries. This focus on capital preservation, coupled with disciplined risk management, has enabled Banorte to sustain its strong liquidity position and support growth initiatives.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of Banorte's operations, with initiatives such as the commitment to plant one million trees by 2030 and participation in the Task Force on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD). Munoz noted that these efforts not only enhance the bank's sustainability practices but also help clients navigate risks associated with nature and biodiversity. As Banorte continues to expand its influence in the financial sector, its commitment to innovation, customer experience, and sustainable practices positions it as a key player in Mexico's economic development.

Jul 02, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte Strengthens Its Position in Mexico's Banking Sector

Grupo Financiero Banorte continues to position itself as one of Mexico's largest banks, combining a traditional branch network with digital services as it competes for retail and corporate customers in a changing rate and regulatory environment. As of 2nd July 2026, Banorte operates in an environment shaped by domestic interest rates, economic growth, and evolving regulation.

Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. (ISIN MXP370641013) is one of Mexico's largest financial groups, with activities spanning commercial banking, consumer finance, asset management, insurance, and pension funds. As a major lender in the Mexican market, the group plays a central role in financing households and businesses across the country. Its nationwide branch and ATM network supports a wide retail franchise, while its corporate and government banking units provide services to larger clients and public entities.

Management attention at Banorte typically centers on maintaining a balance between growth and risk, especially in areas such as consumer credit, mortgages, and small-business lending. Asset quality indicators, such as non-performing loans and coverage ratios, are closely watched, as they show how well the bank is managing credit risk in its portfolio. Additionally, capital adequacy remains a key concern, with banks expected to hold sufficient capital buffers to absorb potential losses and comply with regulatory requirements.

Banorte has invested in digital channels to complement its traditional branch network, offering online and mobile banking for individuals and businesses. These platforms allow customers to make payments, transfer funds, and apply for products such as credit cards and personal loans without visiting a branch. The ability to migrate more activity to digital channels helps Banorte improve efficiency by reducing operating costs per customer while maintaining or even expanding its customer base.

Banorte's shares are listed in Mexico, providing investors exposure to the country's financial sector through a diversified banking and financial services group. The stock's performance over time reflects local macroeconomic conditions, interest rate trends, and the bank's own profitability and risk management decisions. For equity investors, key variables often include return on equity, cost-to-income ratios, asset growth, and dividend policy, all of which shape how the market values Banorte relative to both domestic peers and international financial groups.

Jul 09, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA: A Hidden Gem in Consumer Staples

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. (KOF) is emerging as a potentially undervalued opportunity in the consumer staples sector. As of 9th July 2026, the company stands as the largest Coca-Cola bottler worldwide by sales volume, serving over 270 million consumers throughout Latin America with a diverse product range that includes sparkling beverages, water, juices, sports drinks, and dairy products.

Despite operating in a mature and competitive consumer staples industry, Coca-Cola FEMSA's current market valuation suggests that investors may be overlooking its resilient cash flows and strong profitability. The company's extensive distribution network and established brand portfolio provide a competitive edge, enabling it to generate recurring cash flow.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's intrinsic value-to-price (IV/P) ratio stands at 1.50, indicating that the stock may be trading below conservative intrinsic value estimates. The company's recent financial metrics reveal total revenue of approximately MXN 292.5 billion, operating income of about MXN 40.4 billion, and a net income of roughly MXN 23.0 billion. The firm maintains a strong free cash flow of about MXN 24.2 billion, showcasing its capability to support dividends, investments, and strategic acquisitions.

The company's financial health is further illustrated by its balance sheet, which lists total assets at approximately MXN 314.5 billion and total liabilities at around MXN 160.5 billion, resulting in a solid shareholders' equity of about MXN 154.0 billion. Despite slight increases in leverage due to acquisitions, Coca-Cola FEMSA continues to exhibit strong cash generation, enabling it to navigate macroeconomic challenges such as currency volatility and inflation.

While market concerns such as slowing consumer spending and rising commodity costs persist, Coca-Cola FEMSA's fundamentals remain compelling. With an Acquirer's Multiple of 4.0 and robust operating margins, the company appears to be a promising long-term investment for value-seeking investors looking at the consumer staples sector.

Jul 05, 2026: Coca-Cola Femsa Expands Beverage Operations for Long-Term Growth

Coca-Cola Femsa S.A.B. de C.V., the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the world by volume, continues to leverage its wide Latin American footprint and franchise agreements to drive beverage distribution and long-term growth opportunities. As of the 5th of July, 2026, Coca-Cola Femsa's operations underline a robust business model focused on efficiency and localized strategies that resonate with regional consumer preferences.

Coca-Cola Femsa oversees a broad network of bottling plants and distribution centers that support a high-frequency, high-volume beverage business in both emerging and developed Latin American economies. Its territories include key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, and other countries in Central and South America, where population density and urbanization provide a large consumer base for ready-to-drink beverages. The company manages operations spanning manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, and last-mile delivery to retailers, restaurants, and other points of sale.

The company operates under long-term franchise and bottling agreements that define its rights and obligations to produce, market, and sell Coca-Cola branded beverages in assigned territories. Within this framework, Coca-Cola Femsa focuses on operational efficiency, portfolio management, and local commercial strategies while coordinating with the brand owner on marketing and innovation. This strategic approach allows the company to combine globally recognized brands with local knowledge of consumer preferences and retail formats.

Beyond classic colas, Coca-Cola Femsa manages a broad beverage portfolio that typically includes flavored sparkling soft drinks, still juices, sports drinks, teas, and bottled water. The company adapts flavors, package sizes, and multipack configurations to local consumer tastes and price points, ensuring a tailored approach that meets diverse market demands. Packaging innovation plays a central role in Coca-Cola Femsa's operations, as the company strives to meet sustainability expectations and improve efficiency.

From an investor perspective, Coca-Cola Femsa is often viewed as a consumer staples business with exposure to multiple Latin American currencies and macroeconomic environments. Analysts closely monitor capital expenditure commitments, leverage metrics, and dividend policies when assessing the balance between growth investment and shareholder returns. For many global investors, Coca-Cola Femsa represents an opportunity to tap into Latin American consumer trends through a well-established beverage platform tied to iconic soft drink brands.

Jun 23, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Launches 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle to Enhance Family Consumption

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle, targeting family consumption in key Mexican markets. This launch, taking place on 23rd June 2026, is a significant step in the company's strategy to enhance the availability of reusable packaging solutions.

The Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle is designed for households that prefer purchasing beverages in bulk while maintaining the option for return and reuse. This innovative format not only aims to reduce packaging waste but also lowers the per-liter cost for consumers, who can return the bottle to local corner stores, which have long embraced returnable formats.

Mariana Rodriguez, product manager at Coca-Cola FEMSA, noted that the bottle features a more pronounced waist and a textured grip, enhancing usability at family gatherings. The design is lighter than traditional glass returnable bottles, making it easier for all family members, including children and seniors, to handle. While glass maintains a nostalgic appeal, the PET format provides a modern balance of convenience and tradition.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's CEO, John Santa Maria, has emphasized the importance of refillable packaging as a core strategy. The new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle aligns with the company's sustainability goals, as using refillable containers can significantly reduce the carbon footprint associated with beverage consumption. This initiative not only supports environmental efforts but also fosters a culture of reuse among consumers.

Initially available in select Mexican markets, the Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle leverages the existing popularity of refillable formats. The pricing structure typically includes a deposit for the bottle, making it economically advantageous for families who purchase large quantities. This strategic move is expected to positively impact Coca-Cola FEMSA's long-term cash flow and shareholder value, as the company continues to adapt to consumer preferences while committing to sustainable practices.

Jun 17, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Leverages Logistics-as-a-Service to Enhance Distribution

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. is quietly enhancing its distribution capabilities through Fomento Economico Mexicano's Logistics-as-a-Service offering. This innovative service transforms FEMSA's robust Coca-Cola delivery network into a third-party logistics solution for brands requiring efficient, temperature-controlled distribution across Mexico. This strategic move was made public on the 17th of June, 2026, and is expected to reshape the logistical landscape in the region.

FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service fundamentally allows third-party brands to access the same warehousing, routing software, and last-mile fleet utilized by Coca-Cola in Mexico and other Latin American markets. Clients can seamlessly integrate into FEMSA's extensive delivery network, which significantly reduces the need for them to establish their own complex logistics operations. This means that consumer goods can be efficiently delivered to over 3 million points of sale, utilizing existing routes that serve thousands of small retail outlets daily.

For brands, especially those in the fast-moving consumer goods sector, this service provides an invaluable shortcut to market penetration. Products delivered alongside Coca-Cola benefit from the established distribution patterns that store owners are accustomed to, thus facilitating easier acceptance and integration into existing supply chains. The service's reach can substantially expedite market entry for new energy drinks or healthcare products, compressing lengthy rollout periods into mere months.

Technological infrastructure underpins this service, with advanced routing algorithms and inventory management tools ensuring efficient operations. FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service also offers clients features such as order tracking and delivery proof without necessitating additional investment in software. This is particularly crucial for pharmaceuticals and health products, where stringent temperature control and delivery reliability are essential.

Logistics-as-a-Service is a strategic component of FEMSA's broader vision to maximize value from its existing infrastructure. Although still a smaller segment compared to its core Coca-Cola bottling and OXXO retail operations, it represents a significant opportunity for growth. Investors should note that while immediate scale may be limited, the long-term potential for operating leverage in this logistics venture aligns with FEMSA's overarching objective of enhancing its distribution capabilities.

6.1 Activities

Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. (PINFRA), is a leading Mexican company specializing in the development, operation, and maintenance of infrastructure assets. Its core business activities encompass the management of toll road concessions, airport operations, and railway systems, primarily in Mexico, with a focus on enhancing connectivity and efficiency in transportation networks. The company has diversified into complementary areas such as industrial and urban infrastructure projects, leveraging public-private partnerships to drive growth. Among its fastest-growing segments are toll road concessions, fueled by increasing vehicular traffic and strategic expansions, as well as airport operations, which have benefited from rising passenger volumes and modernization efforts. PINFRA's commitment to sustainable practices and operational excellence positions it as a key player in Mexico's infrastructure sector, supporting economic development through reliable and innovative solutions. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Engineering & construction company by market capitalization.

Director

Director

Luis Javier Solloa Hernandez

Independent Director

In addition, he has been Commissioner and Member of the Board of Directors of various companies within the industrial, commercial and financial sectors. He holds a degree in Public Accounting from Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Mexico, a diploma in Financial Engineering from Colegio de Contadores Publicos de Mexico and a diploma in High Management from Universidad Iberoamericana.

Frantz Joseph Guns Devos

Independent Director

He has worked at Aeropuertos del Sureste, Infraestructura Portuaria Mexicana and Ferrocarriles del Sureste. lseg:urn:newsml:newsroom:20261124:nNRA2u.html_limpio: Directivos de Arca Continental, Xignux y Nestlé México plantearon establecer una política industrial de largo plazo que trascienda sexenios, fortalezca la proveeduría nacional y permita al país competir por nuevas inversiones frente a los incentivos que ofrecen otras economías.Durante la Reunión Anual de Industriales (RAI) 2026, el presidente del Consejo de Administración de Arca Continental, Jorge Humberto Santos Reyna, señaló que para alcanzar este objetivo se requieren tres elementos: infraestructura, talento y certeza para hacer negocios."No podemos estar solucionando las necesidades de energía o de capacidades de agua año por año. Se requiere un plan de largo plazo para poder tener capacidades de poder atraer a esos inversionistas y nosotros mismos como industriales mexicanos, tener la certeza de que vamos a tener las suficientes capacidades para poder seguir desdoblando nuestras empresas", expresó.El empresario indicó que otro de los obstáculos para el crecimiento industrial es la disponibilidad de trabajadores especializados, pues tan sólo en Nuevo León se requieren entre 40 mil y 50 mil nuevos técnicos cada año, mientras que los planteles educativos únicamente forman entre 4 mil y 5 mil.Ante este panorama, destacó la importancia de impulsar la educación dual, mediante la cual los jóvenes combinan su formación académica con prácticas en empresas, lo que les permite acceder a remuneraciones hasta 25 por ciento superiores al concluir sus estudios.Saturación eléctrica limita expansión industrialEn tanto, el director de Asuntos Corporativos de Xignux, David Garza Herrera, señaló que el crecimiento económico del país ha superado el ritmo de desarrollo de su infraestructura, particularmente en materia eléctrica."El crecimiento económico del país, sin duda, ha avanzado mucho más rápido que la creación de la infraestructura. A lo mejor somos víctimas de nuestro propio éxito", expresó.Además, explicó que la saturación de distintos nodos de la red eléctrica de la Comisión Federal de Electricidad (CFE) representa una limitante para la expansión de las actividades productivas.Una de las alternativas, apuntó, es incrementar la capacidad de las líneas de transmisión existentes mediante nuevas tecnologías, aprovechando las torres y los derechos de vía disponibles, sin necesidad de iniciar los trámites que implica construir infraestructura desde cero.De igual forma, consideró necesario establecer incentivos económicos para competir por capitales frente a Estados Unidos, donde Xignux ha recibido apoyos de gobiernos estatales para realizar inversiones.Nestlé pide ampliar base de contribuyentesEn tanto, el presidente ejecutivo y CEO de Nestlé México, Fausto Oliveira Costa, sostuvo que las modificaciones fiscales recurrentes dificultan la planeación financiera de las compañías, debido a que los proyectos industriales se realizan con horizontes de largo plazo.El directivo planteó ampliar la base de contribuyentes para evitar que las necesidades de recaudación gubernamental recaigan sobre quienes ya operan dentro de la formalidad.En este sentido, enfatizó que la complejidad de los mecanismos tributarios genera costos difíciles de anticipar para las empresas, además de incertidumbre respecto a sus obligaciones futuras ante el Servicio de Administración Tributaria (SAT)."Si uno pregunta y dice: ¿y cuánto te va a cobrar el SAT de aquí a cinco años? Ni idea", resaltó.Mercado interno, clave para fortalecer industriaSantos Reyna también advirtió que la relocalización de empresas, conocida como nearshoring, no garantiza por sí sola el crecimiento sostenido de la economía mexicana, por lo que consideró indispensable fortalecer el mercado interno.Por su parte, detalló que alrededor del 95 por ciento de la cadena de valor de Arca Continental en México proviene de las regiones donde opera.Además, destacó que mediante un programa de la Cámara de la Industria de Transformación de Nuevo León (Caintra), en el que participan 26 grandes compañías, se realizan transacciones por más de 400 millones de dólares anuales con pequeñas y medianas empresas (PyMEs)."Una cadena de suministro fuerte no se construye ubicando siempre al proveedor más barato. Se construye desarrollando mejores proveedores", afirmó.El empresario consideró que incrementar el contenido nacional permitirá fortalecer las cadenas productivas y facilitar el cumplimiento de los requisitos comerciales de los productos que México exporta.KL
lseg:urn:newsml:newsroom:20261124:nNRA2u.texto: Directivos de Arca Continental, Xignux y Nestlé México plantearon establecer una política industrial de largo plazo que trascienda sexenios, fortalezca la proveeduría nacional y permita al país competir por nuevas inversiones frente a los incentivos que ofrecen otras economías.Durante la Reunión Anual de Industriales (RAI) 2026, el presidente del Consejo de Administración de Arca Continental, Jorge Humberto Santos Reyna, señaló que para alcanzar este objetivo se requieren tres elementos: infraestructura, talento y certeza para hacer negocios."No podemos estar solucionando las necesidades de energía o de capacidades de agua año por año. Se requiere un plan de largo plazo para poder tener capacidades de poder atraer a esos inversionistas y nosotros mismos como industriales mexicanos, tener la certeza de que vamos a tener las suficientes capacidades para poder seguir desdoblando nuestras empresas", expresó.El empresario indicó que otro de los obstáculos para el crecimiento industrial es la disponibilidad de trabajadores especializados, pues tan sólo en Nuevo León se requieren entre 40 mil y 50 mil nuevos técnicos cada año, mientras que los planteles educativos únicamente forman entre 4 mil y 5 mil.Ante este panorama, destacó la importancia de impulsar la educación dual, mediante la cual los jóvenes combinan su formación académica con prácticas en empresas, lo que les permite acceder a remuneraciones hasta 25 por ciento superiores al concluir sus estudios.Saturación eléctrica limita expansión industrialEn tanto, el director de Asuntos Corporativos de Xignux, David Garza Herrera, señaló que el crecimiento económico del país ha superado el ritmo de desarrollo de su infraestructura, particularmente en materia eléctrica."El crecimiento económico del país, sin duda, ha avanzado mucho más rápido que la creación de la infraestructura. A lo mejor somos víctimas de nuestro propio éxito", expresó.Además, explicó que la saturación de distintos nodos de la red eléctrica de la Comisión Federal de Electricidad (CFE) representa una limitante para la expansión de las actividades productivas.Una de las alternativas, apuntó, es incrementar la capacidad de las líneas de transmisión existentes mediante nuevas tecnologías, aprovechando las torres y los derechos de vía disponibles, sin necesidad de iniciar los trámites que implica construir infraestructura desde cero.De igual forma, consideró necesario establecer incentivos económicos para competir por capitales frente a Estados Unidos, donde Xignux ha recibido apoyos de gobiernos estatales para realizar inversiones.Nestlé pide ampliar base de contribuyentesEn tanto, el presidente ejecutivo y CEO de Nestlé México, Fausto Oliveira Costa, sostuvo que las modificaciones fiscales recurrentes dificultan la planeación financiera de las compañías, debido a que los proyectos industriales se realizan con horizontes de largo plazo.El directivo planteó ampliar la base de contribuyentes para evitar que las necesidades de recaudación gubernamental recaigan sobre quienes ya operan dentro de la formalidad.En este sentido, enfatizó que la complejidad de los mecanismos tributarios genera costos difíciles de anticipar para las empresas, además de incertidumbre respecto a sus obligaciones futuras ante el Servicio de Administración Tributaria (SAT)."Si uno pregunta y dice: ¿y cuánto te va a cobrar el SAT de aquí a cinco años? Ni idea", resaltó.Mercado interno, clave para fortalecer industriaSantos Reyna también advirtió que la relocalización de empresas, conocida como nearshoring, no garantiza por sí sola el crecimiento sostenido de la economía mexicana, por lo que consideró indispensable fortalecer el mercado interno.Por su parte, detalló que alrededor del 95 por ciento de la cadena de valor de Arca Continental en México proviene de las regiones donde opera.Además, destacó que mediante un programa de la Cámara de la Industria de Transformación de Nuevo León (Caintra), en el que participan 26 grandes compañías, se realizan transacciones por más de 400 millones de dólares anuales con pequeñas y medianas empresas (PyMEs)."Una cadena de suministro fuerte no se construye ubicando siempre al proveedor más barato. Se construye desarrollando mejores proveedores", afirmó.El empresario consideró que incrementar el contenido nacional permitirá fortalecer las cadenas productivas y facilitar el cumplimiento de los requisitos comerciales de los productos que México exporta.KL

America Movil S.A.B. de CV (NYSE:AMX) has jumped 21.5% Year To Date. There is uncertainty in the market and it is difficult to predict how economic conditions will be in 2027 and beyond as well as what the impact of those conditions may be on America Movil S.A.B. de CV. However, there are several key reasons why some investors remain bullish on the long-term prospects for America Movil S.A.B. de CV.

Below are some of those key reasons:

- Price/Earnings/Growth of 1.25 versus sector average of 2.9.

- Return on Assets of 4.9% versus sector average of 2.7% and market average of 1.5%.

- Return on Equity of 20.6% versus sector average of 8.3% and market average of 9.5%.

- Return on Capital Employed of 10.9% versus sector average of 8.3% and market average of 3.0%.

- Total Liabilities/EBITDA of 4.3 is less than 5, this compares favourably with the Joseph Piotroski benchmark of 5.

- As per the Du Pont analysis, Return on Equity is high at 20.6%. This is computed as net profit margin of 9.3% times asset turnover [sales/assets] of 0.52 times leverage factor [total assets/shareholders' equity] of 4.2.Also, this has improved from 6.4% last year.

- Tobin's Q Ratio, defined as MCap divided by Total Assets, is 0.8. Compared with the rest of the market the ADR is undervalued.

However, there are also some reasons investors may remain bearish in the long-term including the following:

- The earnings yield of 0.3% is below the 10-year bond yield of 4.58%.

- The price-to-earnings ratio of 344.5 indicates overvaluation compared with sector average of 20.0 and market average of 15.2.

- Net profit margin has averaged 7.5% in the last 3 years. This is lower than the sector average of 9.2% and suggests a low margin of safety.

Company Profile

América Móvil is a telecommunications provider operating wireless and fixed-line networks across Latin America, the Caribbean and Austria and Eastern Europe, selling mobile voice and data, broadband, PayTV and corporate network services under the Telcel, Telmex, Claro and A1 brands. Wireless is the principal revenue source, with 332 million wireless lines at quarter-end, including 153 million postpaid customers, alongside 80 million fixed-line RGUs. Brazil is the largest wireless market at 92.8 million subscribers, followed by Mexico at 81.8 million. Postpaid lines grew 8.9% year over year and broadband accesses 5.6%, the fastest-growing access categories, with Argentina posting the strongest fixed-line RGU growth at 13.8%.
